lines.text: Your computer runs dozens of programs at once: a browser, a music player, a terminal.
Not one of them touches the hardware directly.
Between them and the hardware sits one program with every right: the kernel.
It hands out the memory, the processor's time, the disk and the network.
When a program wants to open a file or send something over the network, it asks the kernel.
That request is a system call. Linux has a few hundred of them.
The kernel checks every request. This program may read that file, not this one; it may never read another program's memory.
Linux is the kernel of most servers on the internet, and of every Android phone.
Keep one idea from this: whoever controls the kernel controls the machine.
